sources.title: GTA 6 Launch Trailer Teases Jason's Troubled Past, a Steamy Shower Scene With Lucia, and Much More
sources.text: Rockstar has released the launch trailer for GTA 6 , which shows us brand new footage of Jason and Lucia as well as the open world. The trailer, which weighs in at 1:30, touches on Jason's troubled past, which involved leaving the army not on the best of terms. We see snippets of a steamy shower scene with Lucia, who is wearing an ankle tag, and plenty of explosive open-world action. Rather than showing gameplay, the launch trailer showcases cinematic action in GTA 6 as it nears its November 19 launch. As per Rockstar's partnership with Sony, the PS5 is prominent in the trailer, with the "plays best on PS5" message displayed at the start. The trailer confirms the footage was "captured on PS5." The trailer begins with some narration from Jason. "I got in some trouble in the army," he begins. "Didn't leave on the best of terms. They don't give loans or anything to people like me." We see a bearded Jason working at Brian's Marina, buffing a boat before he receives a call from Lucia Caminos. Presumably this is the call Jason gets to pick up Lucia from prison. We're shown what look like flashbacks to Jason's time in the army, where he appears to have been in the special forces. We see him wading through water as part of a military unit, and leaping out of a helicopter while on some sort of mission. But these scenes could easily be set in the "present," rather than the past, with Jason gearing up for, perhaps, a police operation. Either way, it explains why Jason is so handy with a gun. We're then treated to various shots showing Jason and Lucia getting up to no good across Vice City, with glimpses of that steamy shower scene. The shot of Lucia wearing an ankle tag could hint at initial restrictions to exploration, as more of the world is opened up during progression through the story, but that's speculation. This week, we learnt about GTA 6's sweat system, and there's a shot in the launch trailer that looks to show this in action. We see a man working out, and he's putting a lot of effort in. Sweat? Yep, it's all there. "Are we gonna be okay?" Lucia asks Jason after yet more explosive shots. "We stuck together through everything," Jason replies. "Just gotta get through it." Here's the official blurb from Rockstar on the GTA 6 launch trailer: We also have confirmation that electronic duo Justice composed the original score for GTA 6. Indeed their track, Flower in a Hurricane, featuring fellow Grammy-winners Tame Impala and SZA along with King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, plays during the launch trailer. It's been a busy week for GTA 6. We've got a report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , details of GTA 6’s sweat system , and confirmation GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards 2026 . Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.title: Over 30 New GTA 6 Screenshots From the Launch Trailer
sources.text: We've put together over 30 screenshots from the GTA 6 launch trailer, showing off Rockstar's open-world in detail. Rockstar surprised fans this morning by dropping a new trailer for GTA 6 . This appears to be the final full trailer for the game before launch, but it paints a picture of the thrilling story. The new trailer highlights some of the more romantic and steamy moments between Jason and Lucia alongside major action setpieces, including one where someone dangles off a payload that is being flown across Vice City. It's pretty over the top, but in all of the right ways. We've put together a slideshow of some of the key images from the trailer, allowing you to take in some details you may have missed, such as the fact that Jason has a dog with him during one of his helicopter rides. You can take a look at the new images down below. Remember, the GTA 6 launch trailer was entirely captured in-game from a PS5, so what you're seeing here is how the game will run on base PS5, not the PS5 Pro. We're yet to see the game running on the Xbox Series X and S. Here's the official blurb from Rockstar on the GTA 6 launch trailer: We are just a little over 30 days away from launch and less than a month away from being able to pre-load GTA 6. Rockstar Games has confirmed that players will be able to pre-download the game starting on November 12, ensuring you'll be fully prepared for the game's release as soon as it becomes available. Despite this seemingly being the final trailer, GTA 6 will still have plenty of marketing beats between now and launch. It's been a busy month GTA 6. Rockstar has been taking over Miami with murals, blimps, and signange . It is even preparing to re-decorate Miami Beach with GTA 6-themed items, such as umbrellas. On November 18, the NBA will host a GTA 6-themed regular season game in Miami with a Vice City themed court, jerseys, and in-person activations . No expense has been spared in marketing this game and we're likely going to see a bunch of other marketing beats in the coming weeks. Meanwhile, we've got a report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , details of GTA 6’s sweat system , and confirmation GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards 2026 . GTA 6 will finally release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. A PC release is also rumored for early 2027 . Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.title: 33 New Details From the GTA 6 Launch Trailer
sources.text: Yet another look at GTA 6 has come our way, which means it’s time to get forensic; we’ve gone through the new trailer with a fine-tooth comb to pick out all of the interesting details hidden within. From peeks at what’s in store for some of its most explosive missions, further insights into Jason’s military past, and more than one visit to a steamy shower, there’s plenty of new things to take a look at. Let’s not waste any more time. Here are the 33 details we spotted in the GTA 6 launch trailer. Multiple shots offer a closer look at Jason and paint a pretty clear picture of the kind of man we’ll be taking control of. We already knew that he was ex-military, but midway through the trailer we see him wearing a U.S. Army T-shirt that offers more details on his service. 1. Firstly, the combat training school Jason seemingly trained at is located in North Fort Law. Longtime fans will recognise this as the military base from the very first Grand Theft Auto game. In that original game, it was located in the state of New Guernsey, but it’s more likely that the one Jason attended is in the State of Alderney, the HD universe’s take on New Jersey. We know that Lucia is from Liberty City, which is located in the neighboring State of Liberty – perhaps they met when Jason was stationed at the base? 2. More prominent than that small print is the word “Marauder,” which matches the skull-and-parachute tattoo on Jason’s arm that we’ve seen in previous videos. The Marauders are presumably the unit he served in, and may be a reference to the real-life Merrill's Marauders, a 1940s special forces group. Its modern-day equivalent is the 75th Ranger Regiment, and so it’s likely that Jason was a ranger. 3. It seems like Jason has fallen on tough times since he left the forces. “I got in some trouble in the army, didn’t leave on the best of terms,” he says in the trailer’s opening. “They don’t give loans, anything, to people like me.” With a situation like that, it’s no wonder Jason has resorted to crime. The cost of living is only going up! 4. Thankfully, it seems like Jason’s experience in the Marauders has equipped him with all the tools for a very fruitful life of crime. We see him wading through water dressed in special forces-like infiltration gear, a pair of night-vision goggles on his head and a silenced assault rifle in his hands. He’s accompanied by two other men, and the trio seem to have disembarked from a boat. While the blush night sky certainly looks very Floridian (or should we say Leonidan), an odd reptile to the left of the scene appears to be a komodo dragon, which is native to Indonesia. Is this a flashback to a mission from Jason’s army days? Or is the reptile simply a native of Leonida’s wetlands, and Jason has perhaps called on some former squadmates to help with some kind of job? 5. Much of the criminal work we see committed across this trailer has something of a military feel to it. We later see Jason on a helicopter, dressed in a bulletproof vest and demonstrating a very professional demeanor. He’s joined by a dog, potentially pointing to not just Jason having a pet, but also being able to use them as some kind of working dog. Later shots also show Jason confidently disembarking a chopper and checking the chambered round in his rifle – all small details, but ones that help paint the picture of a deeply competent professional. 6. Lucia may not have Jason’s highly trained background, but it looks like she’ll eventually adopt at least some of his tactics. A minute into the trailer, we can see her dressed in special forced black and equipped with a Shrewsbury rotary grenade launcher, popping explosives into pursuing police vehicles. 7. She’s demolishing those cars from on high, hanging from the side of some kind of cargo net. A few seconds later, we see a helicopter carrying a giant load in a very similar cargo net – it seems likely that these shots are taken from the same mission, and that Lucia will hang from the net before or after it’s been dragged through the side of a skyscraper. 8. The damage caused by the crash is more detailed than anything we’ve seen in prior GTA games, with hundreds of shards of glass erupting from the side of the building. While this shot alone is far from confirmation that the game will feature Battlefield-like destruction tech, it is a flashy insight into just how detailed Rockstar is able to make environmental demolition. 9. That kind of collateral damage is to be expected from crime on the scale that GTA typically depicts, and it seems like this game has no intention of being smaller than GTA 5’s biggest moments. We can see Lucia leaping off a car onto a commercial liner, suggesting something on the same scale as some of Trevor’s airborne antics. This shot is likely the precursor to the scene in the second trailer that shows Lucia fighting in a plane’s hold as its landing gear deploys. 10. The aforementioned chopper mission is probably a heist, but what’s definitely a heist is the bank job we see. This is actually the vault we previously saw in a screenshot we exclusively debuted back in August , complete with the burning bank notes and Lucia with her hair in a ponytail. 11. For that shot, Lucia is joined not by Jason but by another anonymous character. We can’t see their face, but whoever they are, it looks like we won’t be alone when conducting heists. In a later shot we see Lucia accompanied by gunmen disguised as construction workers, suggesting we’ll often be joined by crews of criminals. But will these be supporting characters introduced as part of the story, or NPCs hired to help, akin to how heist crews worked in GTA 5? 12. While stealing physical money is a tried and tested form of securing dosh, there’s a chance that GTA 6 will toy with a more decentralised approach, too. sources.title: GTA VI’s new trailer gives you one more look at Vice City
sources.text: A “launch” trailer a month before launch. A “launch” trailer a month before launch. The day is almost here, as Grand Theft Auto VI is just about a month away from finally coming out. But before that there’s still one more look from Rockstar Games, which just put out a brief “launch” trailer for the game. It doesn’t reveal much new, but the 90 second clip does give a good sense of the Miami-inflected vibe. It also includes a new track from electronic duo Justice , who are scoring the game. (As with past titles, GTA VI has a huge focus on music .) Rockstar says the new trailer was captured entirely on a PS5. The trailer also includes a brief new description for the game’s story, for those who haven’t been following along closely: Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Of course, if you’re looking for more in-depth gameplay, Rockstar dropped a lengthy “extended look” back in August , which showed off just how cinematic the experience is shaping up to be . Meanwhile, leaks from the game have continued to propagate on the internet, revealing some of the more, let’s say, sensitive elements of the experience . Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19th on the PS5 and Xbox, a solid 13 years after the last GTA — though we might not have to wait quite that long for its inevitable sequel .

sources.title: GTA 6 launch trailer shows a more intimate Jason and Lucia as fans struggle to believe it's real
sources.text: New Grand Theft Auto 6 launch trailer really makes it feel real – we made it The GTA 6 launch trailer is here, formally ushering in the next era of Grand Theft Auto after more than a decade post-GTA 5. Rockstar shared the new trailer earlier today, "featuring the debut of 'Flower in a Hurricane' from original score composers Justice feat. Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard," and confirming that this song will appear on the official GTA 6 soundtrack album. The short trailer sees the dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, open up about their struggles. Jason notably sports long hair for much of the trailer; in the opening seconds, he discusses the obstacles he's faced after a less-than-glamorous military departure. Lucia is seen sporting a monitoring anklet during an intimate shower scene, and at one point wonders, "Are we gonna be OK" amid a storm of crime. Rockstar was in a very helicopter mood with this trailer. One helicopter crashes behind an assault rifle-toting Jason, Lucia rides another through the streets with a grenade launcher in hand, and in a third sequence a chopper is shown carrying a chained load of (presumably stolen) cargo through the city like a wrecking ball, shattering a row of windows on another building. A once-again short-haired Jason emerges from a helicopter in the next shot, only to cut to him and Lucia jumping off a roof into some sort of hotel pool. "Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them," reads the video description. "But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive." The early response from Grand Theft Auto fans is unsurprisingly enormous, with millions piling into Rockstar's accounts across social media. The trailer crossed 1 million views on YouTube in about half an hour, if you can trust overwhelmed metrics. In the comments, GTA 6 hopefuls express disbelief at finally having a launch trailer in their hands. "I thought I would never live this moment," reads one top comment. "We are really at the finish line!!!" says another fan. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Grand Theft Auto 6 is out November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X. The launch trailer was captured on PS5, with a clear PlayStation marketing push bookending it. As if you needed another reminder of why GTA 6 took so long, it has a realistic sweat system that makes Jason and Lucia perspire based on how hard they dance . Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: Some great games to play before GTA VI and Zelda launch
sources.text: Eight new releases including old-school horror, laid-back dressmaking, and the return of Castlevania. You could say we’re in the eye of the storm right now. The storm, of course, being the fall and winter release calendar for new video games. Things started out with a hectic few weeks that were packed with major titles like Control Resonant , Marvel’s Wolverine , Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave , and Gears of War: E-Day . Meanwhile, next month will be dedicated almost entirely to two gigantic games: Nintendo’s remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the long-anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI . But even though things are comparatively quiet at the moment, there are still a handful of great games that have come out recently. Even better: Many of them are short enough that you can easily squeeze them in before your life is taken over by Hyrule and Vice City. Here are eight titles you can check out before things get overwhelming again. Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch, and Steam. This new Castlevania game from the studios that worked on Dead Cells has everything I could have hoped for: intricate levels, challenging platforming, tough bosses, and secrets upon secrets to discover. Sometimes, the game got a little too tough, but thanks to some generous assist settings, I could tweak the experience to be exactly what I wanted it to be. Belmont’s Curse whips. —JP South African developer Free Lives — known for decidedly not-cozy games like Broforce and Genital Jousting — has ventured into the “cozy” space with Dressmaker , a game about designing and sewing dresses, via a small internal team dubbed Cozy Lives. From your small village shop, you take commissions, sketch designs, pick fabrics and accessories, cut the dress patterns, pin them on a mannequin, and sew it all together. There is a lot of creative freedom. You could certainly spend dozens of hours meticulously designing and accessorizing your dresses — I definitely have — but you can also play in relaxed half-hour sessions when inspiration strikes, making it a flexible option in a pretty packed season for games. —KP Available on the Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, and PC. Resident Evil and Silent Hill are as big as they’ve ever been , but if you’re looking for that old-school survival horror vibe, Heartworm is the game. It looks and plays like a long-lost PlayStation classic — you even have limited inventory — albeit with some optional concessions for modern players, like getting rid of the dreaded tank controls. It also has an interesting twist as your character carries around a camera that serves as both a flashlight and a weapon, giving the game its own distinct-yet-familiar feel. —AW As far as co-op puzzle-solving goes, Orbitals doesn’t reinvent the wheel. But it nails the fundamentals, and it does so in a pitch-perfect ’90s anime package that elevates it beyond a stock puzzle adventure. The world and character designs are reminiscent of the peak Toonami days — the timeless art of Akira Toriyama or the stylish sci-fi of Cowboy Bebop — and are gorgeous even if you aren’t particularly nostalgic for the era . It’s short enough to finish in a few sessions, and because Orbitals comes with a “friend pass” that allows someone else to play with you without buying their own copy, it’s easy to get a friend to join you for the journey. —KP Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch 2, and PC. This is a game best explained in relation to things that already exist. It has the 2D exploration of Metroid , controls like a point-and-click adventure, the slow-burning survival horror of early Silent Hill and Resident Evil , and a weirdo Americana vibe that’s clearly inspired by Twin Peaks . That may sound derivative, but Silver Pines is unlike anything I’ve ever played, a detective story that’s a mix of straight-up terror and deliberate and methodical exploration. It even makes you spend (fictional) money to save your game and you can relax with a cup of coffee to increase your stamina. —AW Toem 2 is a sequel to 2021’s black-and-white indie game about photography , and it’s just as lovely as the original. The characters are charming, the quests are silly, and taking pictures is a snap. It was a great travel companion during a recent trip, especially because I was able to finish it over the course of a couple hours. —JP Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch, and Steam. For those interested in video game history, any game with the Digital Eclipse name on it is worth checking out. Even still, a Toy Story collection doesn’t seem as immediately interesting as, say, a history of Karateka or Tetris . But through some fascinating archival material coupled with the actual games, the collection makes it clear how technically ambitious these games were, from squeezing 3D sprites on the Sega Genesis to a surprisingly open-ended A Bug’s Life adventure. Just as important, they’re still fun to play. —AW Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch, and PC. In Well Dweller , an indie Metroidvania from developer Kyle Thompson, you play as an adorable bird in a world filled with cute characters and alarmingly grotesque bosses. The zones are weird and memorable, like a docks level where you jump from dead fish hanging in nets, but they’re a blast to explore, especially because Glimmer’s matchstick weapon cleverly serves double duty as a springboard you can stick to walls. Well Dweller came out of nowhere for me, and it’s easily become one of my favorites of the year. —JP

sources.title: GTA 6 ganha trailer de lançamento e poderá concorrer ao The Game Awards 2026
sources.text: A Rockstar Games surpreendeu os fãs nesta quinta-feira (15) com a divulgação de um novo trailer de lançamento de Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA 6 ) . Publicado sem aviso prévio, o vídeo apresenta novas cenas da história, sequências de ação e detalhes sobre o relacionamento entre os protagonistas Jason e Lucia. O lançamento está previsto para 19 de novembro de 2026 , no PlayStation 5 e nos consoles Xbox Series X e Series S. Com a estreia se aproximando, a Rockstar intensifica a divulgação de um dos jogos mais aguardados dos últimos anos. Entre as novidades do vídeo está uma explicação sobre o passado de Jason. O protagonista revela que enfrentou problemas durante sua passagem pelo Exército e deixou a instituição em circunstâncias desfavoráveis. Segundo o personagem, essa situação dificultou seu acesso a empréstimos e outras oportunidades financeiras, sugerindo que suas dificuldades econômicas podem ter contribuído para seu envolvimento com o crime. O trailer também apresenta perseguições de veículos, tiroteios e outras atividades criminosas, elementos tradicionais da franquia. Outro destaque é o relacionamento entre Jason e Lucia. As novas cenas mostram momentos de intimidade do casal, indicando que a relação terá espaço importante na narrativa. A trilha sonora também ganhou novidades. O vídeo apresenta a música Flower in a Hurricane , do duo eletrônico Justice, com participações de Tame Impala, SZA e King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard. Segundo as informações divulgadas, a faixa integrará a trilha sonora oficial do jogo. Além do novo trailer, GTA 6 está dentro do período de elegibilidade do The Game Awards 2026, uma das principais premiações da indústria de games. De acordo com as regras divulgadas pela organização, os jogos precisam estar disponíveis comercialmente até 20 de novembro de 2026, às 21h, no horário do Pacífico , para participar das categorias principais. Como o lançamento de GTA 6 está marcado para 19 de novembro, o título atende ao prazo estabelecido, desde que a data seja mantida. O jogo poderá ser considerado em categorias como Melhor Direção, Melhor Narrativa, Melhor Direção de Arte, Melhor Trilha Sonora e Jogo do Ano. Entretanto, a elegibilidade não garante uma indicação. A seleção dos concorrentes dependerá da avaliação do júri responsável pela premiação. Caso seja indicado, GTA 6 poderá disputar espaço com outros lançamentos de 2026, incluindo Resident Evil Requiem , Control Resonant e Forza Horizon 6 . Com pouco mais de um mês até sua estreia, o novo trailer representa mais uma etapa da campanha de divulgação da Rockstar e oferece aos jogadores mais uma visão adicional da história que será apresentada na sequência. Rachele Victoria é formada em Letras, MBA em Inovação e atua há 10 anos com comunicação e conteúdo gamer. Amazon Prime também é feito para jogadores! Todo mês, obtenha itens exclusivos, jogos grátis, uma assinatura gratuita na Twitch.tv e muito mais com sua assinatura Prime . Clique aqui para um teste gratuito de 30 dias .

sources.title: Hearing That Dude Say ‘Grand Theft Auto’ At The End Of The Latest GTA 6 Trailer Made Me Feel Like This
sources.text: Earlier today, Rockstar Games released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6. It’s a good trailer that includes some steamy moments between Jason and Lucia . It also features a Grand Theft Auto tradition at the very end: The same dude saying the game’s name at the end in a deep voice. On October 15, Rockstar dropped a new GTA 6 trailer which will likely be used heavily by Rockstar for advertising on TV and elsewhere. And as such, unlike past GTA 6 trailers, this one features a narrator at the very end chiming in to tell you the game’s name and when it will launch, as well as its ESRB rating. You can hear it below. For all the longtime GTA fans, like myself, who have grown up playing these games and getting hyped for each new release, that voice is extremely comforting as we’ve heard it many, many times before. Since Grand Theft Auto 3, each GTA launch trailer has featured, at the very end, seemingly the same dude and his deep voice. In GTA 3 and Vice City’s trailers, Rockstar hadn’t quite nailed the formula yet. But starting with San Andreas, the classic “ GRAND THEFT AUTO …” ending narration had fully developed. Since then, that dude and his voice have appeared in the launch trailers for Liberty City Stories, Vice City Stories, GTA IV, and GTA V . Rockstar has also included this bit of narration in the launch trailers for Red Dead Redemption and RDR2 .Â I was truly surprised by how nostalgic I felt the moment I heard that familiar voice pop up at the end of the new GTA 6 trailer and say: “ GRAND THEFT AUTO 6 . COMING NOVEMBER 19. RATED M FOR MATURE.” I felt like the critic in that famous scene in Ratatouille who, after taking a bite of a dish he loved as a child, was suddenly transported back in time. The moment I heard his voice in that new trailer, I was 13 again. I was watching something on my shitty little TV and seeing the ad for the next GTA game pop up and hearing that guy’s voice. Rockstar only brings out this dude when the game is truly ready to go, so any time I heard it when I was younger, I got so pumped. If you were worried about a last-minute delay, don’t be. The deep voice has assured us all that Grand Theft Auto 6 will arrive on November 19. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. Good luck to everyone else who released a game this year Jason and Lucia bare it all in the GTA6 launch trailer Rockstar has dropped the launch trailer for its upcoming open-world game You've got a little more than a month to check it out before it's gone Rockstar also said it likely won't return to a work-from-home model as too many people want to 'steal' its games Strauss Zelnick eventually understood why it needed more time and provided it

sources.title: Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós”
sources.text: Saulo Camarotti estava explorando uma masmorra no famoso jogo de sobrevivência Valheim quando teve uma ideia: “Essa dungeon sozinha poderia ser um jogo muito legal”, ele relembra em uma conversa com o XBOX Wire. Dois anos depois, esse jogo se tornou real e está sendo lançado como Deep Dish Dungeons no XBOX Series X|S hoje, 13 de outubro, e disponível desde o primeiro dia para assinantes de XBOX Game Pass Ultimate. Em antecipação à chegada de mais um jogo brasileiro ao Game Pass, conversamos com Saulo para explorarmos juntos essa masmorra de Deep Dish Dungeon , talvez até encontrar alguns segredos…. Gênero : Dungeon Crawler/Survivor/Metroidvania Desenvolvedora : Behold Studios Publicadora : Raw Fury Plataformas : Steam, XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e Portátil Modos : solo ou multiplayer até 3 jogadores online Funcionalidades : XBOX Play Anywhere e Cross-Play (Steam e consoles XBOX) Idioma : português Brasileiro nas legendas e interface Em Deep Dish Dungeon controlamos um explorador em busca de tesouros em uma masmorra, sozinho ou na companhia de amigos. E é isso. Uma premissa simples e sem muitos rodeios, já que a ideia, segundo Saulo, nunca foi guiar o jogador para onde ele deve ir. “Eu queria criar uma experiência sobre explorar uma masmorra como um aventureiro e não como um guerreiro”, explica o desenvolvedor. “Não é sobre matar, morrer e ganhar nível. Esse é um jogo em que você tenta entender esse lugar antigo em ruinas e tenta sobreviver”. Com esse foco em exploração, Saulo diz que Deep Dish Dungeon tem uma média de 15 horas de duração até ser finalizado. Enquanto o jogador descobre mais sobre o tesouro que está buscando, e o próprio lugar em si por meio de narrativas espalhadas pelo cenário, surge uma das mecânicas de jogos mais importantes: cozinhar. Já dizia o ditado: saco vazio não para em pé… nem explora, por isso que é fundamental preparar comidas que dão vantagens ao jogador – daí o “Dish” (prato de comida em tradução livre) no nome. “Você come antes de se aventurar. Não é depois, para se curar”, explica Saulo. “E cada categoria de ingrediente no jogo dá uma vantagem diferente, como mais vida ou vigor”. Foi nesse aspecto da culinária que a Behold colocou um tempero de brasilidade ao jogo, com ingredientes como semente de guaraná e mandioca (ou macaxeira ou aipim dependendo da região do país) ou quitutes como coxinha , pastel e bolo de fubá que podem ser preparados. Dá até água na boca. Alguns exemplos de efeito de ingredientes: A própria presença desses ingredientes típicos do Brasil também dá dicas da localização dessa masmorra, apesar do jogo nunca revelar de fato onde é. “O jogo acontece num lugar fictício, mas para nós, internamente, está mais ou menos ali na Amazônia”, revela Saulo. A partir desse conceito, o time se baseou nas criações de elementos de arte e arquitetura que compõe o lugar. Outra caraterística importante em Deep Dish Dungeons é que masmorra que o jogador explora é fixa e não criada proceduralmente. Saulo diz que isso foi uma decisão proposital. Para que cada lugar, obstáculo e segredo foi pensado para dar um senso de progressão que é mais próximo dos jogos no estilo “Metroidvania” do que os de Survival. “A masmorra é toda interconectada que nem um Metroidvania, e à medida que você encontra ferramentas e ganha habilidades, você consegue abrir novas salas e explorar mais a fundo”, explica o desenvolvedor. Essas ferramentas podem ser achadas pelo cenário ou criadas com recurso coletados durante a exploração. Ao obter um martelo , por exemplo, é possível quebrar portas de ferro que antes bloqueavam uma nova área. Já criar um gancho abre possibilidades de agora ir a lugares elevados que podem ter passagens secretas ou dar acesso a novos ambientes. Deep Dish Dungeon é o primeiro título da Behold Studios a chegar no XBOX Game Pass. No Brasil, o estúdio ganhou notoriedade na década passada ao lançar sucessos indies como Knights of Pen & Papper e Chroma Squad , mas Saulo diz que o novo jogo representa uma nova fase para eles, de projetos com produções rápidas e de escopo simples, mas eficaz. O novo game foi desenvolvido em apenas dois anos e por uma equipe de duas pessoas: Saulo na direção, programação e Game Design, e Carolina Baumgarten na arte. Por isso, a visibilidade dada pelo Game Pass foi o estímulo muito bem-vindo para o estúdio nesse momento, como a refeição que dá benefícios antes da exploração da masmorra, ou nessa, caso, do lançamento do jogo. Saulo também explica que estar no Game Pass impulsiona um dos aspectos mais importantes de Deep Dish Dungeon : o multiplayer. Apesar de poder ser jogado sozinho, o jogo foi pensado, desde o início, para ser uma experiência compartilhada junto com outras pessoas em cooperação. “Criar uma comunidade multiplayer nesse tipo de jogo é essencial”, diz Saulo. ““O nosso jogo é multiplayer e cross-play. Então, se você está jogando no Game Pass, pode chamar um amigo que tá no Steam”. Então, reúna seus amigos exploradores, estejam eles no console ou no PC, prepare os suplementos, cozinhe um bolo de fubá e saia para descobrir os segredos e tesouros de Deep Dish Dungeon , que já está disponível exclusivamente nos consoles para XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e no XBOX Game Pass Ultimate.

stories.summary: Just like that pesky Count Dracula, the Castlevania series refuses to stay dead. 40 years after legendary vampire hunter Simon Belmont’s debut, and 18 (!) after the last original 2D entry, Rose Belmont is here to whip undead ass and show that this portmanteau parent to the “Metroidvania” genre of action-exploration platformers can still throw […] The post Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Is a Worthy...

sources.name: Xbox Wire
sources.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Is a Worthy Heir to its Legacy
sources.text: Just like that pesky Count Dracula, the Castlevania series refuses to stay dead. 40 years after legendary vampire hunter Simon Belmont’s debut, and 18 (!) after the last original 2D entry, Rose Belmont is here to whip undead ass and show that this portmanteau parent to the “Metroidvania” genre of action-exploration platformers can still throw down with the best of them. Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is an incredible return to form for the series, standing tall among the many excellent recent games inspired by it. Set in Paris, 1499, Rose is the daughter of Trevor Belmont and Sypha Belnades, whom you may recognize as protagonists of the excellent Netflix animated Castlevania series. Trevor and Rose arrive in Paris, summoned by the Bishop to handle a mysterious evil terrorizing the city, but Trevor is just there to pass the torch (and whip) to his very capable daughter, who’s taking over the family business of carefully exploring a big map full of secrets, accumulating special powers, and murdering a menagerie of mythical monsters. This theme of a generational hand-off is particularly appropriate because Belmont’s Curse is the first 2D Castlevania developed by KONAMI in partnership with Evil Empire, the studio that spun off to manage Dead Cells updates and DLC from creator Motion Twin, who also advised on this project. 2018’s Dead Cells was itself a slick, randomized, run-based twist on the Castlevania formula from the peak of the action-roguelike genre explosion. What it lost in a sense of exploration from the procedural levels, it more than made up for in lush pixel art animation and lightning-fast, buttery-smooth action. Belmont’s Curse inherits that strong aesthetic and mechanical foundation and builds a spectacular edifice of a fixed world on top that allows the game to shine as a cohesive whole, like the bright blood moon looming over so many Castlevania games. I was immediately enchanted by the opening, when Rose and Trevor arrive to find Paris ablaze in vibrant, magenta flames. Where Dead Cells converted rigged 3D animations into pixel-art sprites, Belmont’s Curse makes its 3D models look more graphic and 2D with cel shading, and the results are gorgeous. The benefits really stood out to me when I saw some of the same zombies that I’d been fighting in front of a window in a dark room, rendered backlit in silhouette with a bright red rim highlight, dynamically fading into clearer view as I got closer. Castlevania has always had fun, imaginative design for its enemies and environments, and Belmont’s Curse elevates it with a vibrant and unique visual style. In addition to many returning monsters and characters, there are some fun and surprising French historical figures in the mix, which is appropriate to France as the setting for both the game and the studio that made it. The action is also as good as the series has ever been. 7 types of weapon are available to Rose (longsword, whip, gauntlets, spear, greatsword, sword and shield, and twin swords), each with its own move set to master. Like with Dead Cells , enemy attacks are well telegraphed, providing a satisfying opportunity to develop mastery as you learn to anticipate them. There’s also a parry, which adds a lot of new dynamism to fighting series-classic foes, like in another excellent revival from its peer, Metroid Dread . The Belmont family’s iconic whip also takes on new significance, doing double-duty as a grappling hook. Rose can swing around and zip towards rings throughout the environment, but can also latch directly onto enemies and hurl herself toward them for a devastating attack. This makes both combat and platforming far more kinetic than previous Castlevanias. Rose likes to quip “You’re trapped in here with me!” at the start of the regular arena fights, and that brash confidence is perfectly reflected in her aggressive, fearless playstyle of throwing herself right into danger. All of this culminates in spectacular boss battles, which are demanding tests of your skill, and incredibly satisfying to overcome. I was a little taken aback by how punishing the very first boss was and how much I needed to lock in to defeat him, but it never felt unfair. It’s always thrilling to follow the arc of a boss feeling impossible to learning their tricks and slugging it out – one mid-game boss in particular was about as hard-earned and exhilarating a victory as I’ve had in recent memory Defeating bosses feeds into the game’s other core system: the deck of tarot Arcana provided by Rose’s late mother Sypha. After defeating each boss (or completing certain other puzzles and accomplishments), you gain a spell associated with their Arcana, so each new ability you gain has a flavorful connection to the character from whom you claimed it. It’s also a great example of a game trope I always enjoy: tarot-style archetypes that are not actually from the traditional 22 Major Arcana (see also Cult of the Lamb or Hades II ). You then upgrade those spells through a clever system called Works of Mercy. Each Arcana has 2-3 associated achievements, related both to using the spells in particular ways or completing other deeds in the world. These unlock points to spend on upgrades that improve the spell’s effect, like being able to throw out a second cross boomerang. It’s a great way to take advantage of how achievements encourage players to engage more deeply with a game and tie it back into progression. Absorbing bosses into the tarot deck also has the narrative effect that Rose has freed their spirits from Dracula’s influence and can hear their voices in her head. Some are grateful and eager to aid Rose’s quest, while others mostly mock her. Defeated bosses becoming a peanut gallery in your head providing commentary for the rest of the game is a really fun way to pack in extra characterization. The voice acting is charming throughout—everyone really gets the assignment and chews an appropriate amount of scenery for the series that memorably gave us “W

sources.title: Catálogo de jogos PlayStation Plus para outubro: Mafia: The Old Country, Horizon Forbidden West, Mycopunk e muito mais
sources.text: Dino Crisis 2 e RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 Complete Edition chegam no PlayStation Plus Deluxe. Neste mês, mergulhe no submundo do crime da Sicília do início do século XX em Mafia: The Old Country, enfrente uma fronteira mortal repleta de máquinas impressionantes em Horizon Forbidden West ou encare hordas de inimigos fúngicos com um arsenal extravagante de armas futuristas no jogo de ação cooperativa frenética Mycopunk, todos chegam no catálogo de jogos do PlayStation Plus já em outubro. Enquanto isso, o PlayStation Plus Premium recebe Dino Crisis 2 e RollerCoaster Tycoon 3. A lista completa de títulos estará disponível para jogar em 20 de outubro, salvo indicação em contrário. E, com a chegada da temporada de Halloween, os membros da PlayStation Plus podem aproveitar uma seleção de ofertas exclusivas como parte das nossas comemorações do Horrorfest. Confira os detalhes completos abaixo desta publicação. Descubra as origens do crime organizado nesta conturbada história de máfia ambientada no submundo brutal da Sicília do início do século XX. Lute para sobreviver como Enzo Favara e prove seu valor para a família nesta envolvente ação em terceira pessoa, que se passa em um momento histórico perigoso e implacável. Esta fantástica história ganha ainda mais vida com os visuais impressionantes, a narrativa cinematográfica e o realismo autêntico que consagrou a fama da aclamada série Mafia. A história de Enzo se passa em uma época em que a destreza com uma lâmina de estilete era letal, a espingarda lupara de cano cerrado era a arma de fogo preferida, vinganças sangrentas se prolongaram por décadas e os mafiosos patrulhavam seus territórios a pé, a cavalo ou ao volante dos primeiros automóveis. Acompanhe Aloy ao enfrentar o Oeste Proibido em uma fronteira majestosa, mas perigosa, que esconde novas e misteriosas ameaças. Explore terras distantes, enfrente máquinas maiores e mais imponentes e conheça novas tribos extraordinárias neste retorno ao futuro distante e pós-apocalíptico de Horizon. Reencontre velhos amigos, firme alianças com novas facções em conflito e desvende o legado de um passado ancestral — tudo isso enquanto tenta manter-se um passo à frente de um novo inimigo aparentemente invencível. Fatie alienígenas fúngicos neste jogo de tiro com saque baseado em missões e com altíssimo nível de personalização. Centenas de melhorias feitas à mão, modo cooperativo para 4 jogadores e um pequeno homem-barata. Como não amar? Um esquadrão de robôs rejeitados é contratado pela corporação SAXON e recebe uma última chance de conquistar a glória e alguns lucros (e evitar o ferro-velho). É a Equipe de Risco de Novo Atlas, um esquadrão de exterminadores em frangalhos enviado para descobrir os mistérios por trás de uma catástrofe fúngica que afeta todo o planeta. Embarque numa série de missões perigosas no planeta para afastar a ameaça micológica. Será um simples desastre natural como alegam? E será que a SAXON não fez direito a sua declaração de imposto de renda? Ou foi culpa sua? Mycopunk chega ao Catálogo de Jogos PlayStation dia 20 de outubro. Após um confronto com Huggy Wuggy e libertar Poppy, você deve descer mais fundo na fábrica de brinquedos da Playtime Co. Quebra-cabeças desafiadores e brinquedos horripilantes aguardam. Use ganchos, balance-se e abra caminho com força até a segurança. Tente escapar, e não deixe a mamãe encontrar você. Continue explorando as profundezas da Playtime Co. em busca de respostas. Sua jornada para descobrir o que aconteceu dentro da fábrica está apenas começando… Poppy Playtime: Chapter 2 estará disponível em 27 de outubro. Embarque em The Midnight Walk, uma aventura de fantasia sombria e reverente moldada em argila, criada pelas mentes por trás de Lost in Random, Fe e Ghost Giant. Torne-se o The Burnt One, faça amizade com uma criatura-lanterna perdida chamada Potboy e use a chama dele para iluminar seu caminho por um mundo de contrastes, repleto de maravilhas e horrores. Sobreviva e supere com astúcia os muitos monstros ávidos por devorar a chama do seu amiguinho enquanto vivencia cinco contos de fogo e escuridão, com um elenco incrível de personagens peculiares. Encante-se com cada detalhe perturbador de uma paisagem meticulosamente criada à mão com argila real e animada no estilo stop-motion. Totalmente jogável tanto no PS5 quanto em RV – com o PS VR2. The Midnight Walk estará disponível hoje, 14 de outubro. Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition | PS5, PS4 Por 300 anos, Rena dominou Dahna, saqueando os recursos de seu planeta e privando as pessoas de sua dignidade e liberdade. Nossa história começa com duas pessoas nascidas em mundos diferentes, cada uma procurando mudar seu destino e criar um novo futuro. Com um elenco diversificado de personagens, um sistema de combate intuitivo e gratificante e uma história cativante ambientada em um exuberante mundo pelo qual vale a pena lutar, Tales of Arise oferece uma experiência de JRPG excelente. Tales of Arise – Beyond the Dawn Edition estará disponível em 27 de outubro. Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video Game | PS5 Vivencie a emoção de correr em pistas recém-projetadas que replicam eventos do mundo real e dispute com a mais recente lista de pilotos profissionais: abra o caminho em uma carreira renovada com competições intensas, rivalidades e escolhas estratégicas. Graças ao Unreal Engine 5, aproveite um gameplay renovado com física realista e evolução dinâmica da pista, tornando cada volta única e desafiadora. Domine o fluxo com tutoriais abertos, uma wiki abrangente e assistência de pilotagem da Neural Technology. Monster Energy Supercross 25 – The Official Video estará disponível em 27 de outubro. A pesquisa e desenvolvimento liderados pelo governo continuam para o projeto Third Energy do Dr. Kirk, conhecido por seu potencial em produzir fontes de energia limpa e sua capacidade de destruição em massa. stories.title: House House will not release Big Walk on Xbox in support of pro-Palestinian BDS campaign
stories.summary: Melbourne-based developer House House will not release its co-op hit Big Walk on Xbox, citing support for the Palestinian-led Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) campaign . Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: House House will not release Big Walk on Xbox in support of pro-Palestinian BDS campaign
sources.text: "We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets" Melbourne-based developer House House will not release its co-op hit Big Walk on Xbox, citing support for the Palestinian-led Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions (BDS) campaign . "We have made the decision not to release Big Walk on Xbox, in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS movement's call to boycott Microsoft, and their designation of Microsoft Games (and Xbox) as a priority boycott target," the developer wrote in a statement . "It has always been our intention for Big Walk to be played by groups of friends, and we know that keeping the game off Xbox runs counter to those intentions. This decision means that some people will miss out on playing Big Walk with their friends, and we understand the disappointment we’re causing. We are disappointed too." It continued: "We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets. We've made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world, that coordinated collective action can confront even the most powerful interests, and that one day, Palestine will be free. Thank you for your understanding." House House is not the only developer boycotting Xbox and Microsoft. Dan Dilorio, developer of Luck be a Landlord, asked players not to purchase the game on Xbox and announced plans to donate $10,000 to The Palestine Children's Relief Fund "to (hopefully) offset the revenue the game has generated for Microsoft." Speculative Agency, developer of All Will Rise, expressed interest in joining the No Games for Genocide campaign, which would require returning some Microsoft funding received through "a developer acceleration programme deal." "We would have to ask Microsoft to let us break our contract and somehow make up the shortfall of funds at a time where funding is extremely difficult to come by in the industry," it said in a statement shared with PC Gamer . "Also we would be giving up the opportunity to reach the large audience of players on Xbox, increasing our financial risk and decreasing our potential player pool. The urgency of No Games for Genocide and its value as a growing movement that has the potential to pressure Microsoft to cease its complicity with Israeli genocide won out." Indie developer Ice Water removed Tenderfoot Tactics from Xbox in support of the BDS movement. "We hope that the broader community will join in the pressure campaign and fight for an end to occupation and apartheid in Palestine and across the world." Arkane Studios STJV union members also published an open letter addressed to the heads of the studio, Zenimax, Microsoft, and Microsoft Gaming, demanding that Microsoft stop supporting Israel. The BDS movement started in April 2025 and targeted Microsoft to "end its complicity in Israel's genocide, occupation, and apartheid against Palestinians." After the announcement, over 2,000 Microsoft workers signed the No Azure for Apartheid petition , which demanded the company conduct "a third-party independent audit of our contract, services and product to make sure they are not involved in any human rights violation, be it in Gaza, or elsewhere." In May 2025, Microsoft conducted an internal review . While it acknowledged it provides the Israel Ministry of Defence (IMOD) with "software, professional services, Azure cloud and AI services," it claimed its review found "no evidence to date" that these technologies "have been used to target or harm people" in the ongoing Gaza conflict.

sources.title: GTA 6 ganha novo trailer antes do lançamento com cenas picantes e ação! Assista
sources.text: A Rockstar Games divulgou de surpresa nesta quinta-feira (15) o trailer de lançamento de GTA 6 . Com cerca de um minuto e meio de duração, o vídeo apresenta cenas inéditas de gameplay com Jason e Lucia, além de mostrar mais detalhes da história e das atividades dos protagonistas em Leonida. O trailer traz o que parece ser um flashback de Jason durante seu período no exército, além de sequências de perseguições, tiroteios e momentos de humor. O vídeo também apresenta cenas mais picantes com os protagonistas e mostra personagens importantes para a trama, incluindo Raul e Cal. O novo trailer chega após uma sequência de novidades sobre GTA 6 nas últimas semanas. A Rockstar revelou detalhes sobre a jogabilidade , os controles DualSense , a trilha sonora e uma edição de colecionador , intensificando a divulgação do jogo antes de sua estreia. A divulgação de um trailer de lançamento também responde a uma das principais dúvidas dos fãs: se o jogo receberia um vídeo promocional final antes de chegar às lojas. Embora a Rockstar ainda mantenha parte das informações em segredo, a empresa decidiu apresentar novas cenas com mais de um mês de antecedência. O vídeo começa com um vislumbre da história de Jason, que comenta ter se envolvido em problemas durante seu período no exército. Na sequência, o personagem recebe uma ligação de Lucia, que está na prisão, antes de o trailer avançar para uma montagem de cenas ambientadas em Vice City e outras regiões de Leonida. Entre os destaques estão sequências de ação com os protagonistas, Lucia saltando sobre um avião em movimento e momentos mais íntimos do casal. O trailer também intercala tiroteios e perseguições com situações cômicas, mantendo o contraste entre o tom criminal da história e o humor característico da franquia. Além disso, o trailer de lançamento de GTA 6 também traz a música original “Flower in a Hurricane”, da dupla francesa de música eletrônica Justice com participações de Tame Impala, SZA e King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Segundo a Rockstar Games, o grupo também trabalhou na trilha sonora original do jogo. Lembrando que GTA 6 será lançado em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X|S. O título será disponibilizado exclusivamente nos consoles de atual geração inicialmente — mas é bastante provável que uma versão de PC também chegue no primeiro trimestre de 2027, segundo fortes rumores que circularam recentemente . As informações sobre os horários de estreia, inclusive, você confere aqui ! Claro, a pré-venda de GTA 6 também já está disponível , com duas versões do jogo oferecidas nas plataformas — além da versão física sem disco que gerou polêmicas na comunidade . Ansioso para o lançamento de GTA 6 ? Comente nas redes sociais do VOXL o que achou do novo trailer e quais são suas expectativas para o jogo! stories.title: Reforj developer 4J Studios announces PC release date at Game Republic New Horizons
stories.summary: 4J Studios has announced that its open-world survival sandbox Reforj will be available on PC via a closed playtest starting in Q1 2027. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Reforj developer 4J Studios announces PC release date at Game Republic New Horizons
sources.text: Open-world survival sandbox will be available via a closed playtest starting in Q1 2027 4J Studios has announced that its open-world survival sandbox Reforj will be available on PC via a closed playtest starting in Q1 2027. The news was revealed yesterday at Game Republic New Horizons , during an interview with 4J Studios' Chris van der Kuyl and Joseph "Stampy" Garrett at the conference's VIP reception. 4J Studios shared further details with GamesIndustry.biz , including that the playtest will initially be invite-only "to ensure an optimised player experience" while the studio continues to update Reforj based on player feedback. The developer has not confirmed which platform will host the closed playtest, but will provide this information later in the year with a full announcement. During the session, Garrett emphasised the importance of early access, especially for a game like Reforj. "The things I try to get across for why I think this is a bit different from the more traditional early access route are two main reasons," said Garrett. "The first one I think is just how early we got it in players' hands. We announced it when we had a prototype, so it was only nine months after development on the actual game began, and we literally had a world that could be generated, and it was creative mode building. "There were no survival elements, there were no threats, there was a building. And that's when we announced it, and the very next day after announcing it, we had it in a select group of community members' hands and got them playing. "And then the other way we communicate with the community is every single week we are going through all of the feedback, and we get a lot of it on the Discord, but once again it's not filtered through a community team. It goes directly to Paddy Burns, the CEO and director, and Tom Fyfe, the lead designer. We're going through all of these feedback points, and often it ends up with changes going into the game the next week." The game is currently available to early testers on Xbox Series X|S through its Insider Program. "Xbox really gives you the ability to bring in an audience super early and on a totally solid hardware spec, so you're not getting confused by bug reports coming in and compatibility [issues]." "It allowed us to have a bit of a safe space because everyone out there is a citizen journalist. As soon as you put something out in the world on PC, it may get shared early on. We knew what was coming from our audience, our fans that love 4J and love what 4J did with what they call the legacy console edition. We wanted to make sure that when we really unleashed it on PC, the game was going to be ready for it." In addition to the early access launch of Reforj, 4J recently debuted a technology called Rixels , which offers an alternative way to provide textures while using a fraction of the memory. Rixels are integrated into 4J's proprietary Elements Engine. As creative director Brian Gomez explained to GamesIndustry.biz , the studio developed this engine to create its own sandbox games after porting Minecraft to consoles and handhelds.

sources.title: 2026's Bloodiest Game Just Got a Release Date
sources.text: The Raid-inspired beat-'em-up Acts of Blood arrives in December While big gaming showcases like The Game Awards are packed full of big-budget games, they usually feature plenty of exciting indies, too. Acts of Blood was spotlighted at last year's Summer Game Fest , and it immediately piqued our interest. It's a martial arts beat-'em-up inspired by movies like The Raid . Think Sifu , but with even more blood. On Wednesday, developer Eksil Team announced that Acts of Blood will be released for Windows PC on Dec. 4. It was previously only officially announced for PC, but Eksil Team has good news for console gamers too: Acts of Blood will land on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X sometime in 2027. If you don't want to wait, you can get a taste of Acts of Blood 's combat in its demo on Steam . That demo has over 1,500 Very Positive player reviews , with players enjoying its brutal combat. "Great animations, weighty feeling combat, and simple but meaningful feeling combos," one player wrote in their review . " The Raid is a freaking AWESOME movie and now you can play it," another said . Acts of Blood is like The Raid meets John Wick . You'll play as Hendra as he seeks out revenge, ostensibly by beating up hundreds of dudes throughout various hallways and other locales. Here's its official description: When justice fails, Hendra embarks on a personal quest for revenge that will take him through the bustling streets of Bandapa, Indonesia to uncover the powerful group behind his family’s murder and make them pay for their actions. Learn, develop and improve Hendra’s combat skills, unlock punishing new moves, and become a martial arts master to beat down waves of enemies, defeat powerful bosses, and avenge your family. It started as a solo project from developer Fajrul FN, but his friends gradually joined over time, leading to Fajrul FN taking charge of the small indie team Eksil Team. Last summer, I chatted with Fajrul FN about developing Acts of Blood and its inspirations. "For gameplay, it’s a blend of Sleeping Dogs ’ counter-based combat and Sifu ’s layered combo mechanics. We’re also taking visual cues from games like Max Payne and Manhunt , especially when it comes to grit and tone," he said. Martial arts is at the core of Acts of Blood 's gameplay, with a variety of strikes, counters, and finishers available. There will be an improvisational element too, as you can attack with melee weapons, pick up firearms, and use the environment against foes. "We’re going all-in on violence as a core part of the experience. Brutal takedowns, dismemberment, and yes, our own version of X-ray kills," Fajrul FN said. "We’ve been clear with our partners from the start: this isn’t going to hold back." To any of us who have enjoyed the brutality of action movies like The Furious or fighting games like Mortal Kombat , that's music to our ears. Acts of Blood will start throwing hands on PC on Dec. 4.

sources.title: Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 review
sources.text: Asus' 20th anniversary edition of the Xbox ROG Ally X is as bougie as the $300 price bump implies. Its additions are very welcome, but that's a lot of cash for a familiar package. PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware. The Asus ROG 20th anniversary lineup has been interesting. Black, gold, and indulgent feels like the tagline here, with the Azoth Extreme Edition 20 and ROG Harpe II Extreme Edition 20 containing actual gold, and a fitting price tag to boot. For any criticisms I may have, I don't think you're paying primarily for the branding on the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20, though. You get a new OLED screen which is bigger and brighter than the IPS panel in the standard Xbox Ally X, TMR thumbsticks, refined triggers, a new cooling system, and with that screen comes a snappy 0.2 ms response time. Refined is a good word for the device as a whole. Coming a year later than the last model, the software is smooth and intuitive, and it's easy to swap between Xbox and Windows mode, though it still doesn't feel like a console in practice. For my money, it's the best ROG Ally on the market right now, but the memory crisis has skewed the price of all gaming gear, and the X20 is certainly not the best value as a result. ✅ You want a beefy OLED handheld: OLED handhelds are still fairly niche, and with recent price bumps, I'd pick this over the Legion Go 2 or OneXPlayer's offerings. ✅ You want power on the go: I'd suggest a significantly cheaper handheld if you are after low-intensity games and don't particularly care for big-budget ones. For your Cyberpunks and your Horizons, you will want a Z2 Extreme chip or better to play them at a decent resolution and settings. ❌ You're fine with IPS: $300 more for the X20 over the X is pretty steep, especially if you aren't dying to play on an OLED. ❌ You live in the UK: The pricing on the X20 is not as good value in Britain, with the superior G3-equipped MSI Claw being only £100 more (though no OLED) and the standard Xbox Ally X £400 less. Asus' 20th anniversary edition of the Xbox ROG Ally X is as bougie as the $300 price bump implies. Its additions are very welcome, but that's a lot of cash for a familiar package. 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible The Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 (or should I say XBOX) is a relatively granular update on the Xbox Ally X . I noticed it immediately when putting the two devices side by side, but when it comes to performance, you're getting identical experiences. They have the same chip, the same memory, the same storage. That's the Ryzen Z2 Extreme, 24 GB LPDDR5X, and 1 TB PCIe 4.0 M.2 2280, respectively. Given you don't get a performance bump, you've gotta really care about the details to consider the X20. Arguably its biggest upgrade is the OLED panel, and it is a beauty. The DisplayHDR True Black 1400 certification isn't just for show, as it pops, appearing both bright and ultra-vibrant. It's also got a bigger screen, which does make the device more immersive, but also larger and chunkier. You can technically upgrade the plain old joysticks in the ROG Xbox Ally X with a TMR module with a bit of know-how, but slapping in your own OLED screen would be very difficult, and I certainly wouldn't trust myself to do such fine electronic surgery. Therefore, I do see value in an upgraded, refined, and pretty older brother of last year's device. It's also got a whole new cooling system for frostier temps. You also get smaller upgrades here, like the ability to pull up and turn the D-Pad to make the corner buttons more or less pronounced, plus greater grooves on the face buttons to stop jagged edges, and a combination of more clicky bumpers and smoother triggers. These all combine to make the X20 feel more thoughtful in approach, and given the price bump, it sort of has to do that. The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products The X20 doesn't come with a charger in the box, which makes sense from an e-waste point of view, but it does mean you will get lacking plugged-in performance without an appropriately speedy charger. For instance, I ran the device at 35 W mode and did some of my benchmarks before realising I wasn't getting the full-fat 35 W mode because my charger wasn't quick enough. Could you say that's my fault for not seeing the low-power pop-up from Asus' software Armoury Crate? Absolutely. Does that mean you may need to pick up a quick charger if you want full-wattage plugged-in performance? Also, absolutely. The box for the X20 also comes with a cardboard stand, which doesn't feel as luxurious as the device itself but is clean, effective, and environmentally conscious. It's a small but decent addition that I've been using consistently since unboxing the device without any problems. There was a brief period when the original Asus ROG Xbox Ally X was the highest-performing gaming handheld money could buy. That was until the launch of the much more expensive MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ CG3EM (catchy name, I know) broke onto the scene. Despite launching a year after the original Xbox Ally X, the X20 sees no difference in power (as it has identical specs), and therefore my performance figures are more or less the same as what Dave got in his review of the standard Xbox Ally X. I got a little less in Metro and a little more in Horizon and Cyberpunk 2077, with lower 1% lows in F1 25. In a handful of games, with upscaling on and off (35 W plugged in) I left the GPU memory budget at 8 GB, flicked the device onto its 35 W Turbo mode, and had a good time in F1 24, Horizon Zero Dawn, and Metro Exodus without any upscaling. sources.title: Xbox Ally X 20 vs Xbox Ally X: A wickedly bright OLED screen and frosty temps make for a begrudgingly attractive upgrade for the Asus handheld
sources.text: All that glitters might actually be gold. So, you've seen the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 in all its black and gold glory and wondered if it's worth paying $300 more for it. Well, the answer is 'it really depends on what kind of device you are looking for' and 'how much is a fresh OLED screen worth to you?' Unlike the other ROG 20th anniversary edition bits of Asus gear, the X20 is not about superfluous add-ons (unless you pick up the bundle with XR glasses). You aren't getting a commemorative faceplate here, or extra stickers. You get an OLED screen, TMR thumbsticks, improved thermals, and MicroSD Express compatibility. You also get Impulse triggers, which means they can rumble independently, and the D-Pad can be flicked around to make the corners more or less pronounced. The screen is perhaps the biggest sell here, with its 1400 HDR-certified display going up to a peak brightness of 1,400 nits. As I found in my review , it's so sizzlingly bright at points that I looked at the sun in Cyberpunk 2077 while lying in bed one night and actually winced. Check out the full differences below. 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible In a handful of games and productivity apps (35 W plugged in) With both devices featuring the same chip and memory, you can expect more or less the same performance. In my testing, I got lower Metro performance and worse 1% lows in F1 25, but better performance in Horizon Zero Dawn, Cyberpunk 2077 and 3DMark, so the framerate differences overall just about balance out. I also noticed the X20 never went above 49 watts, which means I would feel more comfortable cranking up the wattage. It helps that its thermals are much improved. Recorded in HW Info whilst performing gaming benchmarks (35 W plugged in) The X20 comes with a refined new thermal cooling system, and it's more than just a marketing term. I recorded temps up to 17 °C cooler compared to the previous model, and even in long gaming sessions, I couldn't manage to push the system's temp above 80°C with its included wattage modes (between 17 W and 35 W). Importantly, I never felt that heat on my fingers as I played, making it a relatively frosty gaming device. Recorded using PCMark 10's gaming battery life test (25 W) In stress testing gaming benchmarks, the X20 managed 2 hours and 9 minutes in the 25 W gaming mode, and almost 3 hours in the 17 W mode. Importantly, it can get up to 9 hours of indie gaming on the go, in my experience. The standard X model has the exact same size battery, so you can expect a similar battery life, though our testing saw it perform a little under the X20. The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products Though you're getting similar performance figures, the day-to-day use of the Ally X20 is superior from my experience. The screen is gorgeous and super bright, all the buttons feel superb under the fingers, it's super quiet (unless you want it to be loud), and it looks phenomenal. As well as all of this, those frosty temps mean you can shove up the wattage if you want, or just have a ton of headroom to avoid throttling in the future. I would really struggle to want to spend over $1,000 on any gaming handheld right now, but if I were flush with cash, I would be majorly tempted to pop the X20 in my basket. If you already have the Xbox Ally X, I wouldn't recommend spending another $1,300 to get a better screen, thermals and TMR sticks (plus some little extras). If, however, you're deciding between the two, I can say that the new additions are very welcome and make for a refined, desirable device. If you've got the cash to splash, it's a sweet device. It's just a shame that the memory crisis has killed handheld market prices. 3.
